title: 'Open and Operating': The Data Behind Trump's Hormuz Claim Tells a Different Story
narrative: On Tuesday, President Trump posted on Truth Social: 'The Naval Blockade remains in full force and effect. The Hormuz Strait is open and operating. All water mines have been removed or detonated.' The same morning he posted a map labeling the Strait of Hormuz 'NEW U.S. Territory,' and in the Oval Office he claimed 'total control over the strait.' Energy Secretary Chris Wright has a theory for why the shipping data doesn't back this up: 'many private businesses undercount the number of ships leaving the Strait of Hormuz.' The private businesses — Kpler, UKMTO, Lloyd's List, JMIC — are the ones counting actual ships. Their numbers tell a different story.
telemetry: Trump (Truth Social, Tue Aug 18): 'The Hormuz Strait is open and operating. All water mines have been removed or detonated' (CNBC, CBS News)
Same morning: Trump posted a map labeling the strait 'NEW U.S. Territory'; Monday in the Oval Office he said 'We control it... We have total control over the strait' (Iran International, CBS)
Trump also threatened to 'bomb the s**t' out of Oman if it blocked the war's end (CBS)
Energy Secretary Chris Wright (Aug 12): oil exports through Hormuz at ~9M bpd, claiming 'many private businesses undercount the number of ships leaving the Strait of Hormuz'
Kpler data: 5-day average of ~13 vessel transits on Aug 12 — a near three-month low, ~90% below the pre-war average of ~130 ships/day (CNBC)
Reuters (Aug 17): five commodity vessels transited Saturday; NONE registered Sunday, versus 31 the prior weekend; one VLCC transited with AIS switched off
UKMTO (7 days to Aug 14): 75 outbound/76 inbound full transits; AIS-visible traffic ~90% below pre-conflict; IMO Traffic Separation Scheme remains suspended
Route split (UKMTO): 19 outbound on the northern (Iranian) corridor vs 8 on the US-coordinated Omani route; 26 inbound northern vs 5 southern

gCaptain/JMIC: 16 of 18 projectile strikes since Jul 6 occurred in the Omani corridor; operators shifting to Tehran's PGSA-run northern route, which demands permits: 'No vessel is permitted to pass through the Strait of Hormuz without a valid passage permit issued by the PGSA'

JMIC has issued warnings/coordinates for at least two mines in/near the TSS and says 'active mine clearance operations are ongoing' — contradicting 'all water mines have been removed or detonated' (BBC, gCaptain)
Iran's new security chief Mohsen Rezaei (Aug 18) mocked the claim on X with a Washington-to-Hormuz distance map: 'Some dreams are too far from reality' (Livemint)

Narrative flip: Trump now says no talks, but envoy Jared Kushner had described 'very positive and active conversations'; Iran's FM says talks never began and the MoU's 60-day window is 'irrelevant' (Livemint, IRNA via ABC)
analysis:
The administration's Hormuz claim rests on four testable assertions: the strait is open, the mines are gone, roughly 9 million barrels a day are flowing, and the U.S. has 'total control.' Every one of them is contradicted by independent, publicly available tracking data. And unlike the official line, the tracking data is falsifiable — anyone can watch the transits, the AIS gaps, and the mine warnings in near real time.

Start with 'open and operating.' Kpler's five-day average on Aug 12 was about 13 vessel transits a day. The pre-war average was roughly 130. Reuters logged five commodity vessels transiting Saturday and none registered Sunday — against 31 the prior weekend. 'Open' is technically true in the sense that there is no physical barrier across the water. But a waterway that moves zero registered commercial vessels on a Sunday is not 'operating' in any sense a shipper, insurer, or mariner would recognize. The word is doing political work, not describing maritime reality.

Then the mines. Trump says 'all water mines have been removed or detonated.' The Joint Maritime Information Center — the U.S.-led coalition's own hub in Bahrain — has issued warnings with coordinates for at least two mines in or near the Traffic Separation Scheme and states that 'active mine clearance operations are ongoing.' You cannot be actively clearing mines that have all been removed. The contradiction is internal to the U.S. government's own maritime command structure.

Then the oil. Chris Wright's ~9 million barrels per day figure comes with an unusual caveat: he says the private companies that track shipping are undercounting. This is the tell of the entire administration position. When an official's defense of a number is that every independent tracker is wrong — not that his data is better, but that theirs is systematically defective — the burden shifts. Kpler, UKMTO, Lloyd's List, and JMIC do not coordinate their undercounts. They independently register the same collapse.

Then 'total control.' The data shows the opposite of control: the only corridor with meaningful traffic is the northern route run by Iran's Persian Gulf Strait Authority, which requires permits and has declared that no vessel may pass without one. Roughly 80% of the traffic that does move is flowing through Iranian-administered waters. The U.S.-coordinated southern route is where 16 of 18 projectile strikes since July 6 have occurred. That is not control — that is a strait where the adversary sets the terms for the traffic that still dares to move.

The final tell is the narrative flip itself. A week ago the administration's own envoy was describing 'very positive and active conversations' with Iran. Now there are 'no talks or conversations going on, or scheduled.' The claim that the strait is open and normalized is being issued on the same day the administration is denying that diplomacy exists — while threatening to bomb Oman, a country that has done nothing but assist stricken crews. The map labeled 'NEW U.S. Territory' is not a legal claim. It is a rhetorical one, and the shipping data is the rebuttal.

The pattern is consistent: the official line is a claim about intentions and control; the independent record is a record of ships, strikes, mines, and permits. When they diverge this sharply, the record is the story.
verdict: [SIPHONED VERDICT]: 'Open and operating' is a claim about intentions, not ships. AIS data shows zero registered transits on Sunday, a five-day average down ~90% from pre-war, mines still being actively cleared per the coalition's own JMIC, and most traffic routed through Iran's permit-controlled corridor. Energy Secretary Wright's response — private trackers are undercounting — is the tell: when the official line and every independent tracker disagree, the tracker is the story. 'Total control' is the one claim the data directly refutes: the strait's busiest lane is run by Tehran.
